hints: Recomputing max for every window is O(n·k). What information from the previous window is reusable?
If a newer element is larger than an older one, can the older one ever be a window maximum again?
Keep a deque of indices with decreasing values: pop smaller values from the back, expired indices from the front.

insight.mnemonic: Newer and bigger evicts older and smaller.
insight.oneLiner: Keep indices whose values strictly decrease; new elements evict smaller ones from the back, expired indices fall off the front, and the front is always the max.

recall.a: To know when the front has slid out of the window.
recall.q: Why store indices instead of values?

recall.a: Values decrease from front to back; all indices are inside the window.
recall.q: What invariant does the deque keep?

insight.why: An element smaller than a later element can never be a future maximum, so discarding it loses nothing. Each index enters and leaves the deque once: O(n).

oneLiner: Keep indices whose values strictly decrease; new elements evict smaller ones from the back, expired indices fall off the front, and the front is always the max.

pitfalls.explain: There are len(nums) − k + 1 windows - start appending once r ≥ k − 1.
pitfalls.title: Wrong number of windows

pitfalls.explain: Check the front of the deque (or heap) against the window's left edge before reading it.
pitfalls.title: Kept a maximum after it left the window

solutions.idea: Take max() of each window slice.
solutions.name: Max of every window

solutions.idea: Push every element; before reading the top, pop entries that are outside the window.
solutions.name: Max-heap with lazy deletion

footnotes.text: Anything smaller than a newer element is dominated forever: it leaves sooner and is never larger. Popping it keeps the deque decreasing, and every index is pushed and popped at most once - O(n) total.

solutions.idea: Maintain a decreasing deque of indices; its front is the current window maximum.
solutions.name: Monotonic deque

statement: A window of size `k` slides over `nums` from left to right, one position at a time. Return the **maximum of each window** position, in order.
title: Sliding Window Maximum
